q5.answer: The live dedup state is a key-value store with one key per event_id. Each value records the received_at, the partition day, and the ID of the micro-batch that claimed the event. Each key expires 8 days after it is set through its per-key TTL, and later copies do not reset that expiry.

q6.answer: The collector does not consult the dedup store, so it keeps accepting batches and appending them to the log, and clients' events are still durably stored. The live consumer pauses and writes nothing it has not checked, so lag grows, and the 14-day log retention covers the pause. The raw archive keeps running, and any outage longer than 14 days would leave a gap on the live path.

q7.answer: Live rows are inserted in one transaction per micro-batch with an idempotency key built from the consumer group and the offset range, so a retry of the same offset range cannot insert the same rows twice. On restart, the consumer re-reads from its last committed offset, and events already claimed by the same batch ID are kept rather than treated as duplicates. The plan does not spell out whether the offset commit happens inside the warehouse transaction or separately.

q8.answer: Replay reads only the raw archive objects under raw/received_day=YYYY-MM-DD/ for partitions D-7 through D, duplicates included. Rebuilt rows are written to a staging table tagged with the replay run ID, and after validation one warehouse transaction swaps them into partition D of events_clean, so dashboards never see a half-rebuilt day.

q9.answer: For each event_id, replay keeps the copy with the earliest received_at, breaking ties by lower collector node ID and then lower batch sequence, and it keeps only the winners whose winning copy was received on day D. Because retries arrive within 7 days of the first copy, every event with a copy on D has its first copy no earlier than D-7, so reading partitions D-7 through D is enough.

q10.answer: Before the swap, the only writes are to the staging table, and events_clean is untouched, so a failed run leaves the live partition as it was. The swap is one transaction, so a failure during it leaves the old partition in place. The plan does not specify how the operator cleans up an orphaned staging table or releases the replay lock after a crash partway through, so the recovery procedure is undecided.
